direct_exposure.basis: One ACTIVE placement on specialty-marine-broking, the chain's money corner (position 4). The placement carries a current PASS fresh-context placement audit (data/mappings/hormuz-maritime.json placement_audits[], issuer_id AON, audited_at 2026-09-06T15:41:00Z), which is the admission path this row uses: the mapping's own census-level audit (audited_at 2026-09-14, status FAIL) is blocked on 12 OPEN links and unrelated placement findings, none of which name AON's specialty-marine-broking evidence. Role evidence is Aon's own head of marine for Asia, quoted directly on the Hormuz closure's effect on the hull war market (Insurance Journal, 2026-03-06).

disclosed_theme_revenue_pct.basis: No Gulf-marine-specific revenue percentage is disclosed anywhere on disk for Aon; the chain's own bottleneck note states the Gulf marine book is a small slice of a diversified broking revenue base, which the exposure argument rests on rather than a measured share.

capture.basis: The chain scores specialty-marine-broking capture at 62 ('the broker takes a share of premium and none of the claim... the shipowner can move between brokers but not around them for a Lloyd's placement'), held at the middle anchor because placement is competitively bid among the same few names. Aon's own FY2025 operating margin of 25.28 percent (companyfacts, official_source true) is the highest of the three brokers this batch examines (WTW 23.48 percent, AJG uncomputable), consistent with a broker capturing real commission economics at the firm level, though the specific Gulf war-risk line is not separately disclosed anywhere on disk.
capture.what_would_change_it: A disclosed marine war-risk commission dollar figure, or evidence the same rate surge is being competed away in the broking fee itself rather than just the underlying premium, would sharpen this from a firm-level margin proxy to a link-specific measurement. Neither exists on disk today; the chain's own capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin field says the same thing.

heat.basis: Ember scores specialty-marine-broking UNDISCOVERED: impact 62 ('commission scales with a premium base that moved by roughly an order of magnitude on this route'), crowdedness 30 ('the brokers appear all over this occurrence as quoted market commentators and nowhere as the trade... not one cited source frames a listed broker as a beneficiary'), capture 62. MEDIUM bottleneck because placement is competitively bid and the Gulf marine book is a small slice of diversified broking revenue, which the screen and this basis both size honestly as undisclosed.

quality.basis: Ten of twelve canonical fields carry a sourced number; quality.piotroski and quality.beneish_state are state NOT_APPLICABLE under Ron's 2026-09-15 broker quality exception (method section 6A): data/market/AON.json's own quality blocks are PENDING_DATA on nothing but cost_of_revenue_fy (piotroski) and cost_of_revenue_fy plus sga_fy (beneish), inputs an insurance broker's income statement never carries. Net debt to EBITDA of 2.62x is the highest leverage of the three brokers in this batch (WTW 1.69x); operating cash flow to net income of 0.94x and FCF margin of 18.73 percent are both healthy and unremarkable for a broking model.
quality.counterweight: 2.62x net debt to EBITDA is real leverage, not alarming for an insurance brokerage but the least clean balance sheet of the three names promoted in this batch. The quality NOT_APPLICABLE exception substitutes structural companyfacts absence for a computed score; it is not equivalent to a strong measured Piotroski/Beneish read, and Stocky's earnings-quality veto must apply the same broker basis wording, not silently pass a blank field.

expectations_gap.basis: The reverse DCF in data/market/AON.json quality.reverse_dcf solves an 12.39 percent five-year implied FCF CAGR against an achieved three-year revenue CAGR of 11.25 percent, a raw gap of 1.14 percentage points. Per method section 7 that raw gap is smaller than the horizon spread itself (4.4 points, from 12.39 percent at five years to 7.99 percent at ten), so this is a statement about the reverse-DCF's horizon convention, not a claimable pricing gap. Recorded honestly rather than rounded up: unlike HUBBELL or a genuine expectations-gap name, Aon's market-implied growth sits close to what it has actually delivered.
expectations_gap.horizon_caveat: Any gap claim on this name below 4.4 percentage points is a horizon-convention artifact, not a price statement, per method section 7.
expectations_gap.assumption_caveat: The discount rate and terminal growth in the reverse DCF are assumed, so both reverse_dcf fields are tagged SPECULATIVE in the confidence audit; this dimension records the measured state only, the deep-dive stage adjudicates whether price is wrong.

Admission rests on the placement-level PASS audit specific to AON, per CLAUDE.md's 2026-09-04 screen-row rule, not on the mapping's overall census status.

The mapping's census-level audit (2026-09-14, status FAIL) remains open on 12 links unrelated to this placement; while AON's specific citation is not itself named as a finding, the mapping as a whole has not reached COMPLETE, so the census cannot yet corroborate this placement beyond its own dedicated 2026-09-06 audit.
